newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Oil's six-month current profits nosedive.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Oil's six-month current profits nosedive.

text.p: Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd said on Friday its parent current profits for the six months to September plunged 73.1 percent from the same period a year ago to 2.57 billion yen.
The sharp decline was due to an erosion in prices for paraxylene and other petrochemical products, said Yoshitaka Muto, managing director for the major oil firm.
Of the total current profit for the half year, about one billion yen was generated in the firm's petrochemical division.
Mitsubishi Oil had originally projected its profit in the petrochemical sector would be three to four billion yen, he said.
A time lag in passing increases in crude oil import costs on to wholesale prices of oil products was another reason for the profit slide, Muto said.

It takes about one or two months for oil firms to pass on fluctuations in crude oil prices to wholesale prices for their products. When crude prices are on the rise, this delay works against oil companies.
Lost profit by the time lag was estimated at around two billion yen, he said.
Mitsubishi Oil forecasts current profits of eight billion yen for fiscal 1996/97, he added.
